elements.content: Grammar focus: So, Such, So Much, So Many.

Look at what follows. An adjective or adverb on its own takes so. A noun phrase takes such, with a or an if the noun is singular countable. A quantity takes so much or so many according to countability. Then add that plus the consequence if the sentence needs one.

so + adjective — intensifies an adjective: the report was so late
such + a + adjective + noun — intensifies a noun phrase: such a long meeting
so much + uncountable — quantity, uncountable: so much noise
so many + plural — quantity, countable: so many errors
so / such ... that — consequence: so late that we missed the deadline
such + plural or uncountable — no article: such errors, such noise
Guided practice: choose the correct option.
1. Complete: 'It was ___ good offer that we accepted.'
2. Complete: 'There was ___ traffic that we walked.'
3. Which sentence is correct?
options: The film was so boring that we left.
The film was such boring that we left.

elements.content: Read and listen: three examples in context.

The report was so late. — So before an adjective alone. (So + adjective.)
It was such a long meeting. — Such with a noun phrase. (Such + a + adjective + noun.)
There were so many errors. — So many with countable plurals. (So many + plural noun.)
What do you observe?

So intensifies an adjective or adverb alone: so late, so quickly. Such intensifies a noun phrase: such a long meeting, such errors. With quantities, so much goes with uncountable nouns and so many with countable plurals. The so ... that and such ... that patterns introduce a consequence. So is never used before a noun, and such never before an adjective alone.
1. Which word goes before a noun phrase?
2. Which goes with an uncountable noun?
State the rule in one sentence, without looking at the table.
Freer production: I can talk about excess and sufficiency.

Success criteria:
- I can use so with an adjective alone.
- I can use such with a noun phrase.
- I can choose so much or so many by countability.
Role play: put your position in ninety seconds; your partner notes every use of the target structure.
Frequent errors and correction:

❌ It was so long meeting that we left (so before a noun phrase) → ✅ It was such a long meeting that we left
❌ There were so much errors (much with a countable plural) → ✅ There were so many errors
Correct these sentences: say what is wrong, then give the right version.
Acceptable variants:

The queue was so slow that we left.
It was such a short notice period that nobody applied.
So much paperwork, so little time.

- Individual: five sentences with the structure, on the topic of the lesson.
- Pair: a ten-line dialogue where so, such, so much, so many carries the argument.
- Group: a six-minute debate, two sides, the structure required in every turn.
- Professional audience: transpose the structure into a memo.
- Academic audience: transpose it into a paragraph of analysis.
